propositions: Creating a ticket directory and writing its first event are not atomic: if the writer dies after os.makedirs but before os.replace, an empty directory remains visible to fsck as MISSING_CREATE and FOREIGN_STORE_PATH

The fix stages both directory and CREATE event in a dot-prefixed temporary path (.tmp-newticket-<pid>-<uuid4hex>) which is invisible to fsck scanners by existing naming convention, then publishes them atomically via os.rename under the write lock

Three store write sites share the vulnerable mkdir-then-write pattern: _prepare_event (called by both single-event and batch paths), inbound_translate._write_event_file, and dispatch_one BRIDGE_ALERT emission; all are converted to use atomic staging

Stale staging directories from dead writers are reclaimed at ticket-create start via sweep_stale_staging using process-start-time stamps to defeat pid recycling, touching only .tmp-newticket-* paths never ticket directories or event data
Concurrency is preserved: distinct pid/uuid suffixes ensure concurrent creates do not collide, and event visibility is delayed until after the write lock and rebase guard pass
Event format and committed layout are unchanged: canonical bytes flow through the staging helper and are renamed into place with identical I2 filenames and directory contents
